question.problem:
Consider the equivalence relation $∼$ on $C,$ defined by $x∼y$ if ${x}^{2}={y}^{2}.$ Which of the following are in the equivalence class $[-4]?$

I. $-4$

II. $4$

III. $4\text{i}$
question.worked_solution:
The equivalence class $[-4]$ consists of the elements that are equivalent to $-4$ under the given equivalence relation. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[-4] & ={x\in C\,|\,x∼-4} \\  & ={x\in C\,|\,{x}^{2}=(-4)^{2}} \\  & ={x\in C\,|\,{x}^{2}=16} \\  & ={-4,4}.\end{aligned}
$$

We see that $-4$ and $4$ are in $[-4],$ while $4\text{i}$ is not.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only".
